title: Registers and counters
kicker: ENEX 152 · Digital Logic · Registers and Counters
subtitle: Line up flip-flops and you can store a word, shift it, or count with it.

sections.title: Registers
sections.body: An n-bit register is n D flip-flops sharing one clock: on each clock edge all bits load in parallel. A load-enable input decides whether the register takes new data or holds. Registers are how a CPU keeps values between steps.

worked.why: A 16-bit register has how many flip-flops?

questions.prompt: Without a load-enable, a register built from D flip-flops would…

choices.text: Take new data on every clock edge.

responses.title: Correct.
responses.body: It could not hold a value.

sections.title: Shift registers
sections.body: Connect each flip-flop’s Q to the next one’s D: on every clock edge the word shifts one place. Serial-in/serial-out delays data by n clocks; serial-in/parallel-out turns a bit stream into a word (and the reverse converts parallel to serial, used in UART/SPI). Shifting left multiplies by 2; right divides by 2.

worked.why: 0110 → value doubles, dropping the old top bit.

sections.title: Asynchronous (ripple) counters
sections.body: Chain T flip-flops (T = 1) so each one clocks the next: the first toggles every clock, the second every two, and so on — the outputs count in binary. An n-bit counter has 2ⁿ states and its top bit runs at f/2ⁿ. Drawback: the change ripples through, so outputs briefly show wrong values (glitches) and the max clock is limited by the delay of n stages.

sections.title: Synchronous counters
sections.body: In a synchronous counter every flip-flop shares the clock and logic decides which toggle: bit k toggles when all lower bits are 1. No ripple, so it is faster and glitch-free at the cost of a few AND gates. Up/down counting just changes that logic.

questions.prompt: Why is a synchronous counter faster than a ripple counter?

choices.text: All flip-flops change on the same clock edge.

sections.title: Modulo-N counters
sections.body: To count 0…N−1, detect the state N and immediately reset (asynchronous clear) or load 0 (synchronous). A decade (mod-10) counter detects 1010 (10) and resets to 0000. Number of flip-flops needed: n = ⌈log₂ N⌉.

sections.title: Ring and Johnson counters
sections.body: A ring counter circulates a single 1 round an n-bit shift register: n states, and each state is decoded by one bit (no logic). A Johnson (twisted-ring) counter feeds back the inverted last output, giving 2n states with the same flip-flops.

questions.prompt: An n-bit Johnson counter has how many states?
